analyzed_vuln.description: `htmlParseSystemLiteral` computes `startPosition = CUR_PTR - BASE_PTR` and later duplicates `len` bytes from `BASE_PTR + startPosition` via `xmlStrndup`. The parser advances with `NEXT` while scanning the literal, but this function only checks `CUR_PTR < BASE_PTR` once before the loop and never revalidates pointer bounds before `xmlStrndup`. With malformed/non-UTF8 HTML input that perturbs parser cursor state during DOCTYPE external ID parsing, `BASE_PTR + startPosition` can become an invalid global address and `xmlStrndup` performs an out-of-bounds read (ASan global-buffer-overflow in memcpy).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered in the `html` fuzz harness (`fuzz/html.c`) when parsing a crafted document containing a `<!DOCTYPE ... PUBLIC ... "...">`/system literal sequence. Data flows: `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` -> `htmlParseChunk` -> `htmlParseTryOrFinish` -> `htmlParseDocTypeDecl` -> `htmlParseExternalID` -> `htmlParseSystemLiteral`. The input must reach `htmlParseSystemLiteral` with a quoted system literal and malformed byte patterns that desynchronize parser cursor/base assumptions, so `xmlStrndup(BASE_PTR+startPosition, len)` reads outside valid input memory.
